department: School of Environmental Studies / Department of Earth Sciences

deadline.value: International Fall 2027 application deadline is May 1, 2027 (document submissions due June 1).

also.quote: International Application Deadlines | Fall | Application | Document Submissions | May 1 | June 1

gre_general.value: GRE scores are no longer required (waived) for all concentrations in the Environmental Sciences Ph.D. program.
gre_general.quote: GRE is now waived for the Environmental Sciences Ph.D. program.

also.quote: NO LONGER REQUIRED - GRE scores of at least 300 (Quantitative + Verbal) and 3.5 (Analytical Writing) for students entering any concentration within the Environmental Sciences Ph.D. degree program.

gre_subject.value: ETS offers no GRE Subject Test in Earth & Planetary Sciences.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: A graduate faculty member must have agreed to direct the student's doctoral program (with signed Graduate Advisor Acceptance Form) and financial support must be identified for admission with full standing and GA consideration.
supervisor.quote: In addition, a graduate faculty member must have agreed to direct the student's doctoral program and financial support must have been identified for a stipend and for research needs. Please click here for the form: Graduate Advisor Acceptance Form (PDF)

also.quote: All concentrations except chemistry require a signed Graduate Advisory Acceptance Form included with their application materials in order to be considered for a Graduate Assistantship.

funding.value: Competitive EVS Graduate Assistantships provide a $2,000/month ($24,000/year) stipend with full tuition and fee waiver (committee meets in March/April, decisions usually by April 15; full admission required first).
funding.quote: Stipend amount is $2,000/month or $24,000/year with a full tuition and fee waiver.

also.quote: The EVS PhD Graduate Review Committee meets once a year in March or April to make decisions on assistantships and continuations for current students.

entry_route.value: Requires a bachelor's or master's degree in science, mathematics, engineering, or environmental science with minimum 3.0 GPA.
entry_route.quote: Applicants for admission to the doctoral program in Environmental Sciences must have: | a bachelor's or master's degree in science, mathematics, engineering, or environmental science;

notes: Geosciences concentration (ENV-GEOS) of the interdisciplinary Environmental Sciences Ph.D. in the School of Environmental Studies. EVS Graduate Review Committee meets in March/April for assistantships (decisions usually by April 15).
name: Environmental Sciences, Geosciences Concentration, Ph.D.
